title: Stem-and-leaf & frequency polygons
examples: How do I make sure my stems are in the right order?
What is the difference between a stem-and-leaf plot and a frequency polygon?
Can I use back-to-back plots for different groups of data?

explain.say: Today we will learn about stem and leaf plots. These plots help us show data in an organized way. We use them to see the shape of a set of numbers.
When making a stem-and-leaf plot, the stems must always be in increasing order. This keeps your data neat and easy to read. For example, if your stems are 1, 2, and 3, you write them in that order.

draw.label: Stems must be in increasing order

explain.say: Now let us look at back-to-back plots. These plots compare two different sets of data. You put one set of stems on the left and the other on the right. This helps us compare two groups easily.
Consider two classes' test scores. One class has stems 15, 16, and 17. The other has stems 14, 15, and 16. You arrange the stems so they go up from 14 to 17 on both sides.

faq.q: What is the purpose of using a stem-and-leaf plot?
faq.a: It helps you organize raw data so you can see its shape. You can quickly spot patterns or gaps in the numbers.
asks: Why do we use stem-and-leaf plots?
What does this plot help us see?

faq.q: If I have data like 45, 48, and 51, what is the stem?
faq.a: The stem is usually the leading digit, so here the stems would be 4 and 5. The leaves are the remaining digits.
asks: How do I find the stem?

faq.q: Why must the stems always be in order?
faq.a: If the stems are not ordered, the plot becomes confusing. It makes it very hard to read the data correctly.
asks: Should the stems go up or down?
Is the order of the stems important?

faq.q: How do I read a back-to-back plot?
faq.a: You read the stems in the middle, and then read the leaves outwards from the stems. You must remember which group belongs to which side.
asks: What is the process for back-to-back plots?
How do I compare two groups with this plot?

faq.q: Can I use this plot for non-numerical data?
faq.a: No, this plot is only for numerical data. It relies on the numbers having a clear order. You need numbers to count and order them.
asks: Can I plot colors this way?

facts: A stem-and-leaf plot organizes data into stems and leaves.
Stems must always be written in ascending order.
Back-to-back plots compare two related data sets.
The leaves represent the final digit(s) of the data points.

quiz.say: Data set: 23, 27, 31, 32. What is the stem for the number 27?
quiz.why: The stem is the tens digit, which is 2 for the number 27.

wrong.0: This is another data point, not the stem.
wrong.2: This is the leaf, not the stem.
wrong.3: This is the whole number, not the stem.

quiz.say: If the stems are 5, 6, 7, and 8, what is the correct order?
quiz.why: Stems must always be written in increasing order from smallest to largest.

wrong.0: The stems must follow a continuous numerical sequence.
wrong.1: The smallest stem must always come first.
wrong.3: This is in descending order, which is incorrect.

quiz.say: A back-to-back plot compares scores from Group A and Group B. If the stems are 5, 6, 7, the correct arrangement is:
quiz.why: You must list all common stems in the middle, in order, for both groups.

wrong.0: The stems must always be written in increasing order.
wrong.1: You must include all stems present in either group.
wrong.3: You must include all stems present in either group.
